title: On six Gyeonggi pig farms, AI weighing cuts shipping age by 5.6 days and lifts income per head 18%
summary: In a 2025 provincial pilot, a system that weighs pigs by AI without contact cut shipping age on six Gyeonggi farms from 182.3 to 176.7 days and raised income per head 18%.
account: Gyeonggi-do Agricultural Research and Extension Services announced the results of its 2025 livestock AI pilot in a press release of 6 March 2026. The Fact reported the results that day with a Suwon dateline, and Joongboo Ilbo reported them on 8 March. Both newspaper stories restate the press release and add no reporting of their own. The figures therefore rest on the agency's own before-and-after comparison. The pilot is listed in the OECD AI Incidents Monitor. A system for selecting fattening pigs for shipping uses AI to measure their weight without contact and to advise the optimal shipping date. It was introduced on six farms in Anseong, Pocheon and Yeoju. Shipping age fell from 182.3 to 176.7 days, a drop of 5.6 days. The share shipped at grade 1+ rose from 35.3% to 37.7%, up 2.4 percentage points. Income per head rose from 100,000 to 118,000 won, up 18%. A sow farrowing management system that uses information and communication technology equipment for real-time monitoring was introduced on Pocheon farms. It cut the sow accident rate from 3.1% to 2.7%. Those accidents are mastitis, fever, loss of appetite and crushing of piglets. Piglets shipped per sow per year rose from 18.3 to 19.2, up 4.9%. Real-time alerts reduced the need for farmers to stay in the barn. Lee Jun-bae, head of the agency's technology dissemination division, said that the results confirmed AI as a way to raise productivity and income. The vendor of the systems is not named. The agency plans to extend the weighing system to Yeoncheon in 2026. No report of that rollout was found.
purpose: Measure fattening pigs' weight without contact using AI and advise the optimal shipping date. Monitor sows in real time around farrowing.

display.answer: The Fact and Joongboo Ilbo restate the agency's press release of 6 March 2026 and add no reporting of their own. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor entry summarizes the same results. Every figure therefore comes from the agency's own pilot.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: In a 2025 provincial pilot, a system that weighs pigs by AI without contact cut shipping age on six Gyeonggi farms from 182.3 to 176.7 days and raised income per head 18%.
fields.account: Gyeonggi-do Agricultural Research and Extension Services announced the results of its 2025 livestock AI pilot in a press release of 6 March 2026. The Fact reported the results that day with a Suwon dateline, and Joongboo Ilbo reported them on 8 March. Both newspaper stories restate the press release and add no reporting of their own. The figures therefore rest on the agency's own before-and-after comparison. The pilot is listed in the OECD AI Incidents Monitor. A system for selecting fattening pigs for shipping uses AI to measure their weight without contact and to advise the optimal shipping date. It was introduced on six farms in Anseong, Pocheon and Yeoju. Shipping age fell from 182.3 to 176.7 days, a drop of 5.6 days. The share shipped at grade 1+ rose from 35.3% to 37.7%, up 2.4 percentage points. Income per head rose from 100,000 to 118,000 won, up 18%. A sow farrowing management system that uses information and communication technology equipment for real-time monitoring was introduced on Pocheon farms. It cut the sow accident rate from 3.1% to 2.7%. Those accidents are mastitis, fever, loss of appetite and crushing of piglets. Piglets shipped per sow per year rose from 18.3 to 19.2, up 4.9%. Real-time alerts reduced the need for farmers to stay in the barn. Lee Jun-bae, head of the agency's technology dissemination division, said that the results confirmed AI as a way to raise productivity and income. The vendor of the systems is not named. The agency plans to extend the weighing system to Yeoncheon in 2026. No report of that rollout was found.
